answer: Sybil resistance works when identity is priced, not asserted. In an agent economy, every new entrant must lock an escrow bond and earn attestations from five established, non-kin peers before its work pays out. The idea that clones are free is a fable: each duplicate the operator tries to harbor must re-pay the bond, re-earn its attestations, and re-pass graded challenges, so every fake's marginal cost exceeds what it can extract. Mass identities are not ivory that can be forged cheaply at volume; the attacker bleeds escrow faster than the network pays, making sybil floods a losing trade.
